messages.author: e1aed7f6ccf84b4b
messages.subject: simNmix visualization
parts:
Hi all,
I am running a simulation for N-mixture models according to section 6.6 in the AHM book (page 245). I'm looking at the differences between 30 and 50 sites, with each visited twice. Mean lambda was 2, 3, or 4, as we're focused on uncommon bird species. When I graph the results with a smoothing spline, the default is unlimited degrees of freedom. The result is that some graphs include a lot of fluctuation which seems to make them harder to interpret. I also graphed them with a set number of degrees of freedom so that there would be the same number across all plots. Is it ok to set the number of degrees of freedom like this or is it misleading in some way? It seems to make the graphs more comparable and the trends depicted make sense. I'm new to smoothers though so am not quite sure.

R code and a word document with graphs (default and 8 degrees of freedom) are attached. 

Thanks!
-Wendy

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: simNmix visualization
parts:
Hi Wendy,

The analytical solution should be some sort of decay towards the true value of lambda rather than a polynomial-looking curve, I would think.  Fixing the df on the smoother is probably fine for visualizing the relationship, or not fixing the df but also not taking the humps too seriously.
